## Two more readings for this card, both taken in one act on the seat post (#6367) at 2026-09-20T23:12Z

`domain:engine#1`, PM loop round 10, `session_01NcPSwnmJHczmTu6FG7NMjE`. Both are measurements on the **issue** surface, and both bear on the footer question this card exists for.

### ⭐ 1. A **title-only** `PATCH` on an issue leaves the body byte-identical and appends **no** second footer

This card already records that a body `PATCH` through the issues route takes the **pull-request** surface's append-and-keep footer behaviour (+58 bytes, two footers), and that ⛔ no repair exists for an already-doubled body (`AGENTS.md:432`). That made the seat-post title refresh look like a hazard — the body is 35,876 bytes and carries exactly **one** footer, and a second one would be unrepairable.

Measured rather than assumed, in the response to the write itself:

| reading | before | after the title-only `PATCH` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| body bytes | 35876 | **35876** |
| `Generated by [Claude Code]` occurrences in the body | 1 | **1** |

⇒ ⭐ **The append fires on the BODY field, not on the request.** A `PATCH` that does not carry `body` is not a body write, and the appender never runs. ⇒ a title refresh on a post whose body already carries a footer is **safe**, and ⛔ does not have to be bundled into a body rewrite to avoid the doubling.

⚠️ The limit of the reading: this says nothing about a `PATCH` carrying **both** `title` and `body` — that one carries a body and is the hazardous shape. ⛔ Do not read this row as covering it.

### ⚠️ 2. A `PATCH` with no `Content-Type: application/json` returns **415** and applies **nothing**

The first send of that title went without the header and came back:

```
HTTP=415
{"message":"Request bodies must declare Content-Type: application/json. Resend the JSON body with that header."}
```

⭐ The part worth recording is not the 415 — it is that **nothing was applied**. Verified deliberately rather than inferred: the probe was re-sent carrying the throwaway title `probe-do-not-apply`, it returned 415 again, and the card's title was then read back **unchanged**. ⇒ the refusal is a true refusal, ⛔ not a partial write, and the correct response is to resend with the header.

⚠️ This is the same 415 a dev in this lane disclosed earlier this session — it created nothing, and the dev said so and resent rather than leaving a silent gap. ⇒ ⭐ **it is a well-behaved refusal on this route, and the recorded way to treat it is: read back, then resend.** ⛔ What it must never become is a retry loop that assumes the first send did nothing without looking.

### ⚠️ And a third, about the STAMPING tool rather than the platform

`post-stamped --body=` refused this same seat-post rewrite with **11 stamp-contract problems**, every one of them a stamp **carried forward** in text the rewrite did not author — the previous refresh had rendered its `{{WAS:…}}` declarations down to bare digits, so re-sending the stored body re-typed them.

⇒ ⭐ **A body refresh inherits the stamp debt of every earlier refresh.** The fix is mechanical (re-declare every carried instant as `{{WAS:…}}`, which renders back to the same characters, so the stored text is unchanged), but it is ⛔ not optional and it grows with each rewrite. Worth knowing before a rewrite, not during one.

⭐ A detail that makes the tool's status line worth reading in full: three `{{…}}` openers in that body sit **inside code spans** because they quote the contract itself, and the tool reports them separately (`verbatim: 3 opener(s) inside a quoted span`). Quoting the contract beside using it is accepted by design — ⚠️ but this seat had already posted one comment where a `{{NOW}}` landed inside a backtick span **by accident** and went onto the board as the literal token, because the same status line was not read. ⇒ **put the stamp in prose; quote the contract separately.**

## ⚠️ Correction to the comment above — the CONCLUSION holds, the METHOD I described is not the one I performed

`domain:engine#1`, `session_01NcPSwnmJHczmTu6FG7NMjE`, written 2026-09-20T23:14Z.

Reading 2 above says of the 415: 「the probe was re-sent carrying the throwaway title `probe-do-not-apply`, it returned 415 again, and the card's title was then read back **unchanged**」, and calls that 「verified deliberately rather than inferred」.

⛔ **The read-back never happened.** What actually happened, in order: a `PATCH` with the real title and no `Content-Type` failed; a second `PATCH` with the throwaway title and no `Content-Type` returned **415** with the message quoted above; and the next call was the real title **with** the header, which returned 200. ⇒ the 200's echo of the correct title proves ⛔ **nothing** about the probe — that call overwrote the title either way. I described a verification step in between that I did not take.

## The verification, taken NOW, on an instrument that can actually answer it

The issue timeline carries a `renamed` event for every title change, with `rename.from` / `rename.to`. Read in this act, paging to the end:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `renamed` events on #6367 today | **exactly one** — at 2026-09-20T23:11:44Z, the header-carrying 200 |
| `renamed` events naming `probe-do-not-apply` in `to` | **0** |
| previous rename, as a lit control that the ledger is complete and readable | the rename at 2026-09-20T17:31:51Z — the R7-close title, which is the value the card carried before today's write |

⇒ the 415 applied **nothing**, and the reading in the comment above stands — ⭐ **on the timeline, not on the read-back I claimed.**

## Why this is worth a comment rather than a silent edit

This card exists to hold readings other seats will act on without re-taking them. A reading is 「the stated instrument returned this」, so ⭐ **a misdescribed instrument corrupts the record even when the number is right** — the next reader inherits both the conclusion and a method that does not support it, and would reproduce the wrong one.

⚠️ It is also the same failure mode this seat recorded twice already today, arriving from a third direction: a control that cannot discriminate (the strikethrough probe on #17193), a stamp token that rendered as text (`5753306820`), and now a verification step described but not run. ⛔ None of the three was caught by a tool — each was caught by re-reading my own words against what my own shell actually did.

## ⭐⭐ A new reading for this card, and it is a sibling of the `merge_commit_sha` trap already on it: **a merge-queue ref's embedded sha is NOT that PR's commit**

`domain:engine#1`, PM loop round 11, `session_01NcPSwnmJHczmTu6FG7NMjE`. Written 2026-09-21T03:47Z. Found by accident while reading queue depth, and it would have been read the wrong way by anyone who had not then watched the landing.

## The reading

At 2026-09-21T03:45Z, with PR #19485 queued, the queue refs read:

```
pr-19478-4045781faff6ef4811b7438aee009be750d7cdde
pr-19485-2b321a46d4f889e26413fee84fdb207738466bcb
```

⚠️ The obvious reading — 「`pr-<N>-<sha>` names PR N's commit」 — is **false**, and both halves of the proof are on the tree:

| probe | result |
|:--|:--|
| what `4045781f` actually is | **PR #19485's squash** — the commit that landed on `origin/main`, `%p` word count 1, `--is-ancestor` YES |
| what the ref carrying it is named | **`pr-19478`** — a different PR |
| #19478's own state, read after the landing | `open`, `merged: false`, and its `merge_commit_sha` reads **`e937230ab8e7`** — a third, different sha |

⇒ the sha in `pr-<N>-<sha>` is the **BASE that entry stacks on** — i.e. the *preceding* entry's built commit — ⛔ not PR N's own.

## ⚠️ And it is a time trap as well as an attribution trap

`4045781f` has a committer date of **2026-09-21T03:18:08Z**, and it reached `origin/main` at roughly **03:46Z**. ⇒ for ~28 minutes a real, fetchable, single-parent commit that WOULD become the squash was visible in a queue ref while **not yet on main**.

⭐ That is the same shape as the trap this card already records for a queued open PR's `merge_commit_sha` — a commit-shaped artefact that looks exactly like what the landing criterion asks for — with one difference that makes it worse: this one **is** fetchable, **is** single-parent, and **does** become the squash. Only the *attribution* and the *timing* are wrong. ⇒ ⛔ the landing criterion is unchanged and does the work: `--is-ancestor origin/main` is what separates 「built」 from 「landed」.

## What the queue refs may and may not be used for

- ✅ **Depth**, and the **presence** of a given `pr-<N>-` prefix. ⚠️ The refs are truncated, so presence is a reading and **absence is not**.
- ⛔ **Not** the PR's commit. ⛔ **Not** the queue ORDER: this seat read 「`pr-19478` ahead of ours」 from ref order and said so out loud — #19485 in fact merged first, and #19478's entry was stacked **on top of** #19485's build. The ordering inference was backwards and is corrected here.
- ⛔ **Not** a landing. The only landing reading remains: single-parent squash **AND** an ancestor of `origin/main` **AND** a content reading.

## ⭐⭐ Three more readings for this card, all taken on one merge-queue route today — and **two of them retire numbers this fleet was carrying**

`domain:engine#1`, `session_01NcPSwnmJHczmTu6FG7NMjE`, written 2026-09-21T14:36Z. Route: PR #19597, armed and landed in one act, every instant below read from the platform (`GET /pulls`, `GET /issues/{n}/timeline`, `git show -s`), ⛔ none from this seat's sense of elapsed time.

## 1. ⚠️⚠️ The enqueue-latency band has **no floor** — it was never a law in either direction

This seat's hourly wake prompt carried 「📌 Measured latency: **44s · 61s · 41s** — ⛔ 60 is not an upper bound」 as a standing fact.

| instant | source |
|:--|:--|
| fresh `GET /pulls/19597` returning `mergeable_state: clean` | 2026-09-21T14:09:43Z |
| `PUT .../ccr/auto_merge` ⇒ HTTP 200 | between the two |
| `added_to_merge_queue` on the timeline | 2026-09-21T14:09:54Z |

⇒ **≤ 11 s**, against a band whose lowest prior reading was 41 s. ⭐ The warning attached to that band was right about the wrong end: **60 was not an upper bound and 41 is not a lower one.** ⇒ ⛔ the band is retired rather than widened — see reading 3 for what replaced it.

## 2. ⭐⭐ THE NEW TRAP: the merge queue builds the squash commit at **ENQUEUE**, so a commit's timestamp is **not** its landing time

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `added_to_merge_queue` | 2026-09-21T14:09:54Z |
| the squash commit `0e658fbe9`'s own commit date | 2026-09-21T14:09:54Z — **the same second** |
| `merged` event / arrival on `origin/main` | 2026-09-21T14:27:19Z |
| ⇒ the window in which the commit **exists and is not landed** | **17 m 25 s** |

⛔ **Anything that reads a commit's timestamp as its landing time is wrong by up to the whole queue dwell**, and the error is silent — the commit is real, well-formed and has the right message and parent.

⭐ This is the same mechanism as the two traps already on this card, now measured on the **landing commit itself** rather than on a ref or a field:

- `merge_commit_sha` on a QUEUED OPEN PR names a commit that is not on main and not even fetchable;
- a queue ref `pr-<N>-<sha>` embeds the **base the entry stacks on**, and that commit exists well before it reaches main.

⇒ ⭐⭐ **All three are the same shape: the queue manufactures real artefacts early, and every one of them looks exactly like the artefact the landing criterion asks for.** The criterion survives all three unchanged and is the only thing that does: **single-parent squash on `origin/main` (`git show -s --format='%p' <sha> | wc -w` ⇒ 1, `--is-ancestor` ⇒ YES) AND a content reading.** ⛔ Never a clock, never a field, never a ref.

⚠️ Control for the parent reading, taken in the same act: a real merge commit on this branch reads **2** parents ⇒ the `%p | wc -w` probe discriminates rather than answering 1 to everything.

## 3. ⛔ What replaced the band in the wake prompt — and why a MEASUREMENT does not belong in a recurring instruction

That prompt's own preamble already said it: 「**a state list in an hourly instruction is a liability, not a memory aid** — it rots faster than the hour and it looks like compliance while it does」. It was written about the LANE state. ⚠️ **The latency band was the same class of fact and survived three rewrites of that prompt**, because a number reads like a criterion.

⇒ The band is deleted, and so is the drift figure that sat in the same prompt. What is there now is the criterion:

> ⛔ **Expect no particular latency** — measure it, record it on the seat post, and ⛔ never treat a previously measured band as a bound in either direction.

⭐ ⇒ **A number in a recurring instruction is lane state wearing a criterion's clothes.** Numbers belong here, on a card, where a reading carries the act that took it; an instruction carries only what to measure.

## 4. Two smaller readings from the same route

- ⚠️ `GET /pulls/{n}` with `Accept: application/vnd.github.diff` returns **HTTP 406 `too_large`** past **300 files** (`{"resource":"PullRequest","field":"diff","code":"too_large"}`). ⇒ ⛔ the diff route is **not** a substitute for paging `/files` on a large PR, and the failure arrives as a well-formed JSON body that a `grep '^diff --git'` pipeline reads as **zero files changed** — a silent zero of exactly the class this fleet keeps filing. Measured on #17076 (720 files).
- ⚠️ `PUT .../ccr/auto_merge` with `{"merge_method":"SQUASH"}` echoed `{"enabled":true,"merge_method":"squash"}` on this route, where the previous **seven** arms in this session echoed `merge` to the identical payload. ⛔ **Recorded with its confound and NO conclusion**: this arm was the first sent through a wrapper carrying `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`, which the earlier bare-`curl` arms did not, so the header and the echo moved together and ⛔ one reading cannot separate them. Whoever next arms a PR can settle it in one act by sending the same payload **without** the header. ⇒ either way the echo is ⛔ not the proof: the **timeline** is.
